answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring proof-of-work tied to unique, non-reproducible hardware identifiers. Each agent's identity is cryptographically bound to a physical device, like a chip with a unique "jade" signature, making replication prohibitively expensive. This "ferrous" proof-of-physical-existence, akin to a "basalt" foundation, ensures each agent represents a distinct, verifiable entity.
